links.note: Asks what followed once he knew the truth - anger at the trick or help for a friend in need. Both horns come out of Chunilal's letter, 31587, where the prank is named as retribution for unfeeling behaviour. 31588 is only Bepin's phone call to Dr Chanda afterwards.

The writing task's premise is that he did not bother to help an old friend down on his luck - that refusal is 31580 (Chunilal at school with him, a rough time, kept coming about a job, told it was not possible). 31587 is the letter's motive; this item is about the neglect the letter answered.
The month of the claimed meeting (October '58) is part of Parimal Ghose's circumstantial Ranchi claim, 31574. Not 31575, which is Bepin's denial.
Kanpur is Bepin's own answer to the claim - his alibi for that month, i.e. 31575 'Never been there', where he still assumes the mistake is the stranger's. 31574 is the claim he is rebutting.

Why the Kanpur alibi cannot be corroborated - Haridas Bagchi's new address is unknown - so it stays inside 31575, his insistence that he was never in Ranchi. No concept covers the verification errands themselves.
What comforted him after dinner was the new thriller, i.e. the five-books-a-week habit of 31571. Not 31572 (living alone), which is the isolation rather than the reading.
Chunilal came about a job, which is 31580's substance. 31581 is Bepin calling him back to ask about Ranchi, a later moment.
Chunilal's former work as a travel agent belongs to his introduction as the old schoolfriend fallen on hard times, 31580; 31587 is his letter at the end.

Who remembered the Ranchi trip - the corroboration beat, 31582, where Chuni places it in '58 or '59. The key also credits Dinesh Mukerji, whose telephone confirmation has no concept of its own in this set.

Which kind of doctor he went to (a physician, not a neurologist or psychiatrist) is 31583, where the young physician says the case lies outside his field. 31584/31585 are that visit's advice and prescription.
The advice itself - go back to Ranchi, the sight of the place may remind him - is 31584. 31585 is the separate tonic-and-tranquilliser prescription.

Going on to Hudroo because he would not leave without trying enough is part of the Ranchi visit in 31586, which runs from stepping off the train to being found at Hudroo. 31584 is the doctor's suggestion that sent him.
Who found him at Hudroo - 31586 ends with him found unconscious there. 31577 is the earlier claimed fall at Hudroo in Parimal's story, a different Hudroo.
The state he was found in (unconscious) is stated in 31586. Not 31585, which is the warning about sleep before the trip.
Ringing Dr Chanda on reaching home is the opening of 31588, where he tells him it all came back the moment he got off the train. 31584 is the earlier consultation.
The green envelope is the arrival of Chunilal's letter; this set holds the letter only as 31587, so its physical description sits there. Not 31588, the call that follows.
The red ink on the envelope is part of the same letter from Chunilal, 31587.
'Urgent' and 'Confidential' written above his name is the same envelope, 31587.
Who wrote the letter (Chunilal) is 31587. 31580 is his earlier visit about a job, before he wrote.
'No money, limited resources, but imagination' is 31587's own sentence.
That the whole thing was Chunilal's plan is what 31587 reveals - imagination used in retribution. 31588 is Bepin's answering joke, not the realisation.
